raikot-bridge.story: At Raikot Bridge, a road bridge on the Karakoram Highway spanning the River Indus, you are at the gateway to Nanga Parbat base camp in Diamer District, Gilgit Baltistan, Pakistan. From here, the Karakoram Highway continues all the way up to Khunjerab Pass and into China, or tourists can hire jeeps from the bridge and follow an unmetalled track to Tattu Village, a journey of around 90 minutes. A further three-hour hike takes you to Fairy Meadows National Park. Around the bridge, a small junction village has a few hotels, several small shops and restaurants, and a mosque.
raikot-bridge.name: Raikot Bridge

fairy-meadows.story: Traveller, when you reach Fairy Meadows, locally known as Joot, you will be on grassland near one of the base camp sites of Nanga Parbat in Diamer District, Gilgit-Baltistan, at about 3,300 metres above sea level. From this launching point for mountaineers summiting Nanga Parbat by the Rakhiot face, the point often mistaken for the summit is the North Peak (7,816 m), while the true summit (8,126 m) remains hidden behind the North Peak’s massif and the Silver Saddle. You approach by a fifteen-kilometre jeepable trek from Raikot Bridge on the Karakoram Highway to Tattu, where the dangerous and narrow gravel mountain road is open only to locals who provide transportation, then continue by a five-kilometre hike of about three to four hours from Tato onward. Here in the Rakhiot valley, at one end of the Rakhiot glacier, locals have operated camping sites since 1992, and the six-month tourist season starts in April and continues until the end of September.
fairy-meadows.name: Fairy Meadows

nanga-parbat.story: Traveller, this is Nanga Parbat, known in Shina as Diamer, the ninth-highest mountain on Earth with its summit at 8,126 m above sea level. It lies immediately southeast of the northernmost bend of the Indus River in the Gilgit-Baltistan region of Pakistan-administered Kashmir, and as the westernmost major peak of the Himalayas, it is the western anchor of the entire mountain range. It is one of the 14 eight-thousanders, rising far above its surrounding terrain with the second-highest prominence among the 100 tallest mountains on Earth, known as the Killer Mountain for its high number of climber fatalities and for pushing climbers to their limits; according to Guinness World Records, it is the fastest growing mountain, growing taller at 7 mm per year. Its name comes from Sanskrit nagna and parvata, translating to "naked mountain" and referring to the usually snowless south face, while its Shina name Diamer or Deo Mir means "mountain of God" or "heavenly mountain."
nanga-parbat.name: Nanga Parbat
